title: Prompt Sets & Benchmarks: Onboarding and Regression Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview
This playbook defines Redwood Inference's standards and operational procedures for onboarding prompt sets, running benchmark suites in the eval-harness, and the regression triage process that follows any detected quality degradation. It covers prompt design guidelines, metric selection, pass/fail thresholds, quantization-aware evaluation, and triage/runbook steps for incidents caused by model updates or configuration changes.

Goals
- Provide a repeatable onboarding checklist to make prompt sets production-ready.
- Standardize benchmark execution so results are comparable across models, quantization profiles, and hardware.
- Define clear regression detection criteria and an actionable triage process to minimize user-facing impact.

Scope
This document applies to:
- All prompt sets that will be used by product teams for feature gating, A/B experiments, or automated quality checks.
- Evaluation runs executed in the eval-harness (CI jobs, periodic benchmarks, canary checks).
- Regression triage for quality issues attributed to model/version changes, quantization, or runtime config changes.
Not in scope: one-off exploratory experiments; those should be captured in ephemeral notebooks and, if promoted, follow this playbook.

Definitions
- Prompt set: curated collection of inputs, expected outputs, and metadata (labels, categories, difficulty).
- Benchmark suite: set of prompt sets and evaluation scripts used to measure a model's performance on business-relevant metrics.
- Regression: a statistically significant degradation on one or more pre-defined metrics relative to a baseline model/version.

Ownership and Roles
- Prompt owner: product or ML engineer who authored the prompt set and is responsible for maintaining metadata and correctness.
- Eval owner: applied-ml engineer who configures benchmark runs, validates results, and manages CI integrations.
- On-call (for regressions): SRE/applied-ml rotation responsible for initial triage and page.
- Stakeholders: product manager and feature owner who decide on blocking actions (rollback, mitigations).

Onboarding Checklist (prompt owner)
1. Metadata: ensure each prompt has id, category, difficulty (easy/medium/hard), tags, and source attribution.
2. Expected outputs: include a canonical answer where applicable and multiple acceptable aliases or scoring rules.
3. Size: aim for 100-1,000 examples per critical prompt set; smaller diagnostic sets (10-50) are allowed for narrow behaviors.
4. Sanity tests: run prompts against current production model to capture baseline outputs and expected metrics.
5. Privacy review: confirm no PII or customer secrets (see data-management policy).
6. Add to registry: upload prompt-set YAML/JSON to the eval registry and link in the prompt-set manifest.

Benchmarking procedure (eval owner)
- Test environments: benchmarks must be run in a controlled environment identical to the target deployment (e.g., hosted vs dedicated vs private) or include clear annotation of differences.
- Standard command (example):
  rw-eval run --suite prompt-sets/feature-x.yaml --model redwood/clarity-7b --quantization none --output results/feature-x-clarity-7b.json
- Reproducibility: store seed, model checksum/version, quantization profile, hardware type, and eval-harness version alongside results.
- Run cadence:
  - CI: light-weight smoke on PRs (20-50 examples)
  - Nightly: full benchmark for all registered prompt sets
  - Canary: run new model builds against critical prompt sets before rollout

Metrics and Thresholds
- Metric types: accuracy/exact-match, F1, ROUGE-L, BLEU (where applicable), semantic-similarity (embedding cosine), and calibration metrics (confidence vs correctness).
- Primary thresholds (example defaults):
  - Critical prompt sets: <2% absolute drop on accuracy/exact-match triggers alert.
  - User-facing generative prompts: >5% increase in hallucination rate (as measured by labeller or hallucination detector) triggers investigation.
  - Embedding quality: >0.03 drop in mean cosine similarity vs baseline for retrieval prompts triggers triage.
- Statistical significance: require bootstrap or paired t-test with p < 0.05 for noisy metrics; for small prompt sets use conservative thresholds and manual review.

Prompt Design Guidelines
- Short prompts: keep examples representative of production prompts including system instructions and tool calls.
- Negative examples: include adversarial and edge-case inputs to capture failure modes.
- Canonicalization: normalize whitespace, casing, and non-semantic tokens when appropriate for metric computation.
- Categorization: tag prompts for behavior (safety, factuality, format, retrieval) to allow targeted slicing.

Quantization and Model Variant Considerations
- Evaluate quantized variants separately: include quantization profile used (e.g., int8, q4_0, q8_0) in results metadata.
- Known quantization artifacts: increased tokenization sensitivity, slight reductions in factuality, and larger variance on small prompt sets. Capture these as expected ranges in the quantization profile doc.
- Recommendation: for production gating, require full-suite run on the target quantization profile before approving a rollout.

Regression Detection and Triage Workflow
1. Detection: automated job flags a regression when configured thresholds are exceeded. Alert(s) are routed to the applied-ml-oncall channel.
2. Initial triage (on-call, 30-60 minutes):
   - Confirm reproducibility: re-run benchmark against same model version and runtime.
   - Check CI/infra: look for recent infra changes, quantization conversions, or kernel updates.
   - Narrow impact: identify prompt categories or slices with largest delta.
3. Escalation (if confirmed and customer-impacting):
   - Page product owner and ML lead.
   - If rollout-related, initiate rollback to previous model version and pause canary.
4. Deep analysis (48-72 hours):
   - Root cause analysis: compare logits/token probabilities, attention/embedding drift, and differences in generation traces.
   - Human review: sample failed prompts and collect labeler annotations.
   - Mitigation: temporarily update prompt templates, apply targeted post-processing, or revert quantization profile.
5. Postmortem: publish an incident summary with root cause, timeline, mitigation, and follow-up actions.

Runbook: quick checklist for an on-call responder
- Reproduce failure locally using eval-harness with exact metadata from stored result.
- Check model registry for recent pushes (model ID, digest).
- Look at quantization conversion logs and recent runtime releases.
- If model change: run diff across token-level distributions for a representative prompt subset.
- If infra change: consult release notes for kernel/scheduler updates and coordinate with eng-serving-runtime.

Config / Example Table (to copy into CI job)
- suite: prompt-sets/feature-x.yaml
- model: redwood/clarity-7b@2026-10-30
- quantization: q4_0
- hardware: a100-40gb
- eval-harness-version: 2026-10-01
- seed: 42

Example CI snippet (YAML):
- name: Run feature-x benchmarks
  uses: redwood/rw-eval-action@v1
  with:
    suite: prompt-sets/feature-x.yaml
    model: redwood/clarity-7b@2026-10-30
    quantization: q4_0
    output: results/feature-x-clarity-7b-q4_0.json

Labeling and Human-in-the-loop
- For ambiguous failures or small prompt sets, require human labeling (2+ annotators) and adjudication.
- Maintain a labeling rubric linked in the prompt-set metadata.

Escalation Criteria for Customer Impact
- Any regression that causes a major feature to fall below its SLA or a customer-visible regression on a paid flow should trigger immediate rollback and an on-call page.

Maintenance and Housekeeping
- Quarterly review: prompt owners must review and refresh critical prompt sets.
- Registry hygiene: remove duplicated or deprecated prompt sets with deprecation notices for 30 days.

Appendix: Useful Commands
- Run a focused re-run: rw-eval run --suite prompt-sets/critical-payment-flows.yaml --model <model> --output debug.json --seed 42
- Summarize diffs: rw-eval diff --base results/feature-x-clarity-7b.json --compare results/feature-x-latest.json --out diff-report.html

- Runtime/serving: eng-serving-runtime@redwood.com
